question: Should a title or picture's right-click menu lead with Animate and Add Key?
context: Right-clicking a clip used to show 21 rows. The rework holds each kind to about ten, with the rest under More. The animation mock draws the menu on a title's key line with Animate and Add Key first.

options.label: Keep them under More
options.summary: A title or picture opens with Split, Start and End at the playhead, then Animate In and Animate Out, then Cut, Copy, Delete and Ripple Delete. Animate and Add Key at the playhead are one level down under More.
pros: The menu stays at about ten rows, as you asked on 2026-10-17
Every clip kind reads the same way
cons: Keying a title by right-click takes one more step than the animation mock draws
options.mitigation: The diamond on the clip header and Key at Playhead in the menu bar still add a key in one step.

options.label: Animate and Add Key on top for titles and pictures
options.summary: A title or picture opens with Animate and Add Key at the playhead time, as the animation mock draws, then Split, Start and End, then the deletes. Animate In, Animate Out, Cut and Copy move under More to keep it short.
pros: Moving a title from A to B is one right-click away
cons: Cut and Copy leave the top of the title menu, unlike every other clip
options.mitigation: Command X and Command C still cut and copy a picked title.

answer.note: Taken as recommended: the user, 2026-10-19, said there were too many cards, most did not matter and they could not follow them. Change it later only if they complain about the result
